pages.title: Drawing and coordinates
pages.body:
Coordinates are x right, y down, in mm. Arcs and rotations are clockwise-positive. Chamfer trims both edges by the given distance; fillet creates a tangent arc. Positive offset is outward on closed shapes/circles, left of travel on open paths; arc offset increases radius.
Arcs: choose Arc method in Drawing options. "Center and radius": drag from the center to the start, then click the end direction. Enter a value in the radius box (mm) to fix the radius; then click the center, the start direction and the end direction. "3 points": click the start, a point on the arc, then the end to make the arc through them (collinear points cannot make an arc; Esc cancels).
End and center magnet: while drawing, the cursor sticks to other shapes' endpoints and to circle/arc centers regardless of the Snap checkbox (centers show as faint crosses only while a drawing tool is active). Set the distance with "Magnet distance to ends/centers (px)" in Drawing options (default 10; 0 turns it off; saved). Midpoints, intersections and the grid still follow the Snap checkbox. The midpoint and both ends of a line, of each side of a polyline and of each span of a Bezier or pen curve (the midpoint of a curve is the middle of its length), the midpoint (middle of the curve) and both ends of an arc, the 8 points of a circle (top, bottom, left, right and the four 45° points), and the center of each visible stitching hole and mark also attract the cursor at the same distance (so the Ruler can measure the pitch between holes), regardless of the Snap checkbox; with a drawing tool, these points appear as small diamonds when the pointer comes within about 40 px. In addition, when a center-type point (the midpoint of a side, the midpoint of an arc, the center of a circle or arc, the center of a small loop) is within 40 px, the cursor also lines up with that point straight above/below it or straight to its left/right when within 10 px (horizontal and vertical separately; it wins over the grid; a thin cyan dotted line from the point shows the match; endpoints are not used). Handy for drawing a vertical or horizontal line through a center. Dragging the end handle of a selected line lines up with centers the same way (the center wins over the line's own direction; if the line's extension crosses the vertical/horizontal line through the center, the end lands on that crossing so the line stays straight; the line's own midpoint is ignored). Use it to pull the end of a slightly tilted line onto a center vertical. When you drag shapes to move them, the left/right and top/bottom edges of what you move (groups and multiple selections included) snap to the edges of other shapes, horizontally and vertically on their own (a thin cyan dotted line shows the match). If it catches too much, hold Alt after grabbing: point magnets and edge snapping are off while Alt is held (release to get them back; Shift for horizontal / vertical still works). Setting the snap distance to 0 turns them off as well. When you drag an end handle of a selected line, it also snaps to intersections with other lines. Pulling the end of a line that protruded past an intersection (a short line split off at the intersection) back to the intersection removes that line (Undo brings it back; lines with stitch holes and lines touching nothing are kept). When lines are stacked (same shape, or overlapping along the same straight line, on the same layer, style and color), a warning appears at the top and the overlap is drawn thick red. The "Merge stacked lines into one" button merges all of them at once, each into one line covering the whole stretch (one undo step; places where a line with a stitch path would have to be extended are left alone and reported). That button handles straight lines only. To merge the overlaps of the selection including curves, polylines, arcs and circles, select shapes and press "Merge overlapping lines" in the left menu (also in the right-click menu; Shift+W): edges shared by neighboring cells, doubled lines, the same curve with slightly shifted vertices and the same arc become one, and for overlaps of different colors the colored line is kept. Shapes used by paint, stitch-hole routes, parts or grid records stay as they are.
Fillet (R) and Chamfer (C) work on two lines sharing an endpoint, or on a polyline (e.g. a rectangle) with one click: click near a corner to round just that corner, or along an edge to round every corner with the radius (C distance) in the box. Choosing Fillet or Chamfer shows a small box at the top of the canvas for the radius (C distance); the number stays until you change it and is remembered next time (separately for fillet and chamfer). Nothing happens if it is empty or 0 or less. The result is a chain of lines and arcs, and Undo restores it in one step. It cannot be made when the radius would overlap a neighboring corner, or at the ends of an open polyline. When the line has stitch holes, a small box asks before anything changes: "Keep them" (holes stay where they are; only holes on the cut-off part of the corner are removed; spacing is not adjusted), "Re-stitch" (fixed-pitch and equal-spacing ranges are stitched again on the new line with the same tool and pitch; hand-placed holes stay), "Remove" (stitch holes only) or "Cancel". Nothing changes until you choose, and Undo takes it back in one step.
Rectangle: with the Rectangle tool, drag between two opposite corners (or click, then click) to draw a closed 4-point polyline. Hold Shift for a square. In the entry box, type "x,y" for the first corner and "@width,height" for the second. Nothing is made when the width or height is 0. To draw a rectangle of a given size, choose the Rectangle tool, enter Width (mm) and Height (mm) in the bar at the top of the canvas, and click where you want it. Anchor chooses whether the click is the top-left corner or the center. You can keep placing it, and magnets and snapping work on the click. A faint preview follows the cursor. Leave Width or Height empty to go back to dragging freely. To change the size of a rectangle you already drew, select it with the Select tool. A “Size of the selected rectangle” box appears at the top of the canvas; enter Width (mm) and Height (mm) and press Enter (or Tab to the next box) to resize it. “Fixed point” chooses the spot that stays put when the size changes (top-left corner or center). Press Esc to discard what you typed. Dragging a corner handle also updates the numbers. Only axis-aligned rectangles qualify, and a rectangle with stitch holes cannot be resized.
Offset:first set the Offset distance and Side (outside / inside) in Drawing options. Click a shape to select the part between intersections with other shapes (shown in orange); double-click to select the whole connected shape (a closed shape if it is closed). Setting "Range" to "Outline (outermost contour)" selects the largest contour passing through the click (a closed polyline, or a closed loop of lines, arcs and curves), so you can pick the outline even when cell polylines or fold lines overlap its edge. Press Enter or the Offset button to run it. Connected lines are treated as one, passing through their joints. Closed shapes go outside or inside; open lines go to the left (outside) or right (inside) of travel. The result is a yellow dashed line; change color and line style in the Info card.
Divider line: click near where two lines cross, inside the angle you want to divide. From the nearest intersection, lines (blue dashed, on the guide layer) are drawn that divide that angle into equal parts. In the box at the top, set the number of divisions (2 = bisector, 3 = trisectors), the line length (empty = the shorter of the two bounding arms) and the mark position (mm from the intersection; empty = no mark). With a mark position, a dot mark - the same kind as the Mark tool's - is placed on each line at that distance. Undo reverts the lines and marks in one step. It works with straight lines, arcs and curves.

pages.title: Stitching and editing
pages.body:
Start Stitching from the right-click menu item "Stitch" (or the Shift+S key); it was moved there from the left tool column. Click a start point and then an end point on a line to place holes between them (the points can be anywhere on the line and snap to ends, intersections and existing holes; connected lines are followed as one path). Three placement methods: Fixed pitch = from the start, every pitch, up to but not past the end (no hole is forced onto the end); Variable pitch = holes at both the start and the end with the spacing evened out; Count = enter the number of holes (both ends included) and they are spaced evenly. Margins and an s section measured from the chosen start direction can also be set. Placing again over the same span replaces its holes, and replacing only a section allows mixed tools. Alt/⌥+click places one hole at the clicked position. After you click a start point, moving the mouse shows faintly where the holes would go if that position were the end point (clicking places them exactly as shown), and hovering a line lights up the whole connected path. On a line that runs all the way around (a closed path) there are two spans between the start and the end: the side with no holes yet is chosen automatically (the shorter side if both are empty), and the pitch carries on across the seam; hold Shift while clicking the end point to use the other side. When stitching along a dashed line drawn inside an outline, the start and end also snap to points dropped straight down from the outline's ends and center (within 12 mm), and a ring appears as you approach. Closed paths never duplicate the seam hole; backstitching reuses 2–3 holes. When more than one dashed line (route) passes through both the start and the end point (for example a dashed loop and a dashed line across its middle meeting at the same points), click the end point a little toward the dashed line you want and the route nearest to your click is used. If the click lands exactly on the joint and cannot decide, press Tab before clicking the end point to switch between the available routes (the faint preview holes, the highlighted dashed line and the message at the bottom change; press again for the next route, and after the last one it returns to the first). With only one route, Tab does nothing. When you continue from the end of holes you already punched (the end of a stitched range), the route you were stitching along comes first among equally near routes (Tab switches to another). Where lines cross or meet in a T, the line that carries straight on is treated as one route (for example, a dotted loop joined by a center line, or crossed by short outline marks, still gives you separate left-hand and right-hand routes around the loop); the branching lines are separate routes. Lines you have already stitched are left out, so a route is only the connected part that is not stitched yet. When the start and the end are on different lines that meet at two or more places, the meeting place that gives the shorter run is chosen first, and Tab switches to another one (the faint preview switches too).
Use Select to drag holes freely or constrained to the path. Shift selects multiple holes. Angle, slant and deletion affect selected holes or the selected shape’s whole path. Shape moves and copies include the entire stitch path. Locked layers are protected.
Dots default to 0.5mm diameter. Mark precedence is hole, path, document, tool. Round tools use holeD; an explicit circle mark uses holeW. Tool updates change dimensions but keep existing hole pitch and angle; replace holes to apply these settings. Tools persist in browser storage and document JSON. Matched stitching is STEP 6; SVG/PDF/DXF exports are later steps.
Matching the real iron: in the Stitch card set hole width, height (blade length) and slant to measured values and press Update. "Print test strip" prints 10 holes with a 50 mm scale at actual size to compare with the iron. If an imported drawing (.lcc etc.) uses a small drawing-only tool, reassign its holes to a registered tool so the hole size matches the real iron.
Mark tool: click on a line or curve to drop a dot mark at that spot, one at a time (you choose the start and can mark anywhere along the line). Connected lines are treated as one path and their joints are passed through. Marks are points on the same path as stitch holes; the size is "Dot diameter" in the Stitching card. You can select, move or delete them.
Marking by distance: enter 1 or more in "From the base point along the line (mm)" in the Stitching card to drop a mark that far along the line from a base point. Click the base point (a line end or corner), then click the line in the direction you want (small circles show the possible spots). For the end of an open line the direction is fixed (into the line), so one click is enough. Distance is measured through joints of connected lines, and wraps around on a closed line. Nothing is placed past the end of the line. Set it back to 0 to drop marks where you click.
Diamond angle and diamond / round choice: in Stitching > "Tool editor", set the kind (diamond, European, round), the blade slant (angle in degrees), the diamond width and height, the round diameter, the number of teeth and the pitch, then press Add (or Update). Registered tools appear in "Tool to use". The direction of holes already placed can be set numerically with "Hole angle" in "Hole editing".
Settings sets: in the "Settings sets (save / recall)" card on the right, save the punching, patchwork, offset and other settings together with your registered tools under a name (up to 30 in this browser, newest first). "Recall the selected settings" restores them (tool changes can be undone), and "Export to a settings file" / "Import a settings file" carry them to another computer as a JSON file.
Forward and reverse slant: newly placed diamond holes default to forward slant ("/" on a line drawn left to right). Pick "Reverse (＼)" in the switch under "Tool" for reverse ("\\" direction). Set the size of the slant as a number in the tool editor Angle (forward uses the opposite sign). On vertical or diagonal lines the holes rotate with the tangent.
Changing diamond / round holes afterwards: select the holes (or the lines that carry them) by dragging a box around them (Ctrl+A for everything), then choose "Change diamond / round holes together…" from the right-click menu. In the window pick the new shape (diamond or round), enter the size (width × height for diamonds, diameter for round holes) and press Change: every diamond and round hole in the selection changes at once. Hole positions and spacing stay the same, and "Range to change" lets you choose the target: only the selected holes (the window starts here when you open it with holes only selected) / the holes in the selection (including holes on selected lines) / all holes of the same kind as the selected ones (whole drawing). Holes you did not select are untouched even if they were punched with the same tool, unless you choose "all holes of the same kind". The "Holes to change" checkboxes limit it to diamonds only or round holes only. Turning round holes into diamonds slants them along the line (forward slant); going diamond → round → diamond brings reverse-slant holes back as they were. Undo is one step. Press "Erase holes" to delete the holes (diamond / round) in the same range and keep the lines (tick only Diamond or only Round under "Holes to change" to limit it; Undo is one step).

pages.title: Pen (continuous Bézier)
pages.body:
Bezier tool: click the start, click midpoints (any number), then double-click the end (Enter also finishes). A smooth curve passes through every clicked point, and you can edit nodes and handles afterwards. Right-click also edits via points (on the curve: add one there; on a via point: remove it).
Click for corner nodes, drag for smooth nodes with handles, as many as you like. Enter or double-click finishes; clicking the first node closes the path. Esc removes the last node.
Select a single pen shape with the Select tool to show its nodes. Drag nodes or handles (Alt/⌥ breaks one side of a handle). Double-click on the curve to add a node, Delete removes the chosen node. Use “Smooth / corner” in the Info card to switch. Lines, Béziers and polylines can be converted with “To pen path”.

pages.title: Text and dimensions
pages.body:
The Text tool asks for the text after you click its position. Size and angle are edited in the Info card. Select one text and a dotted frame and a square handle appear at its top-right corner; drag the handle on the drawing to change the text size (mm) without moving its base point (release to confirm, one undo step, minimum 0.5 mm, also works while the Text tool is active). The Text tool's "Font" box (Gothic, Mincho, Rounded gothic, Handwriting style, Monospace) sets the font of new text. To change it afterwards, select one text and pick a font in the Info card, or select the text (several are fine, and so is text placed from a phrase) and choose "Text font and size…" from the right-click menu, enter the font and size and press Change (items left as "Keep" do not change; one undo step). How a font looks depends on the fonts installed on this computer (a similar one is used if missing). SVG and print follow the font; PDF prints only half-width letters and digits and ignores the font. For the text color, select one text and pick it in the Info card ("Back to default color" removes it); in the right-click window tick "Change color too" to change several at once. It shows on screen, in PNG (color), SVG and print (black in black-and-white output; near-white becomes black when printing on paper).
The Dimension tool takes two clicks and draws a dimension line with the value in mm. Click a rounded corner (an arc, a Bézier or a polyline curve) to pick it, then the next click decides the radius (R) dimension of that corner: click inside the circle for a line from the center to the curve, or outside the circle for a leader out from the curve (length = the dimension offset; the second click's direction sets the line's direction). Esc picks again. A click that snaps to an endpoint starts a distance instead. The offset is set in the "One at a time" part of the Dimensions card and can be edited later. Text and dimensions are ignored by stitching and offsetting.
The "All at once" part of the Dimensions card adds, in one go, the overall width and height of each piece, the length of each straight edge, circle diameters, radii of rounded corners and arcs (R) ("How to draw R" chooses a line from the center, "inside", or a leader out from the curve, "outside") and stitch spacing (per range that differs from the tool selected in the stitching card: one span line labelled "stitch ○○ mm ×n") (tick what you want; only the selected shapes when that box is ticked; places that already have a dimension are skipped; overall width and height at the widest point of each piece = connected lines; no overall size for slots and holes inside a piece; symmetric edges on one side only; dashed lines and the marks layer are skipped). Drag a dimension line to move only the line (the measured points stay and it aligns with nearby dimension lines); the offset can also be typed in the Info card. Hold Shift while dragging to move the whole dimension. "Remove all auto dimensions" keeps the ones you drew by hand.
The Ruler tool shows the distance, horizontal, vertical and angle between a start and an end point you click (it snaps to endpoints and centers; Shift = horizontal / vertical). Nothing is added to the drawing.
The "Phrases" card stores reusable text (brand, item name, size, date; multi-line) by name in this browser. "Place on drawing (click)" puts it at the clicked point, one text shape per line, on the Guide layer.Phrases also remember their font and text size (choosing a phrase puts them back into the fields; "Save" remembers the current values again). "Export" saves phrases.json; "Import" on another PC merges it (same names are replaced).

pages.title: Numeric entry
pages.body:
Type in the field at the bottom and press Enter. Formats: “x,y” (absolute), “@dx,dy” (relative to the last point), “len<deg” (from the last point, clockwise positive), or a plain number for radii.
Line: start point, then end points (keeps chaining). Circle: center, then radius. Arc: center, radius, start angle, end angle. Polyline: points, then Enter on an empty field. Dimension: two points.
To rotate the selection, press Rotate on the left (key Q). A small angle box (clockwise is positive) appears at the top of the canvas; enter a number and press Enter or Rotate to turn the whole selection about its center. Esc closes the box.

pages.title: Layers and the Info card
pages.body:
Choose the drawing layer, visibility, lock and name in the Layers card. Defaults are Pattern, Hardware and Guide: Pattern = cut lines, Hardware = outlines and holes of placed hardware, Guide = everything that is not a physical part (text, dimensions, dashed lines, stitch lines, underlays, marks). Shapes on locked layers cannot be selected.
The Info card shows coordinates, length, radius and angles of the selected shape; editing a value updates the shape, and stitching holes follow.
The Info card also lets you pick a shape color (blue, green, red, white or yellow) and line style (solid or dashed); not available for text, dimensions or fold lines. These are reflected in SVG, DXF and PDF export. Importing a .lcc file maps its original colors (Aqua=outline to blue, Lime=patch lines to green, Orange=dimensions and Yellow=marks to yellow) onto these five colors automatically.
Changing several shapes at once: Shift+click, or drag over empty space to box-select (shapes that fit entirely inside the box are selected; Ctrl/⌘+A selects all). A group you made with Group is selected whole by a click, but a box selects only what is inside the box (shapes of the same group outside the box, and their holes, are not moved or deleted); sets the app made itself, such as hardware and fold-section drawings, are still selected whole. To select just one shape of a group, Ctrl+click it (⌘+click on Mac), for example to delete only a circle of a patch (when a circle has a cross of lines, click the circle line itself; then Del removes only that one). Hardware and fold-section sets stay whole even with Ctrl+click. To select only the outline (outermost contour) lines, select the patch or shapes and press "Select outline only" in the left menu (also in the right-click menu). Only the lines of the closed contour (including doubled lines) are reselected; inner lines, circles and cells are not. If you select only the patch (cells), the frame around it (the outline the grid was made in) is selected, and if the selection has no contour of its own, the contour in the drawing that surrounds it is selected. Then change "Line color" in the Info card to change only the outline (the drawing itself is not changed). If the contour has a break it cannot be found: use "Close gaps" first. Double-clicking a line of a group selects the whole connected outline it belongs to (double-click again with that outline selected to pick just one line). With two or more selected, the Info card shows only Layer, Color and Line style; changing one applies to every selected shape in a single undo step. Setting Line style to Dashed moves them all to the Guide layer. A blank field means the selected shapes have different values. With the Select tool, a click selects only the part between intersections, Alt+click selects only the part between two stitch holes (the line is split there; Ctrl+Z undoes it), and double-click selects a whole connected chain (lines, arcs and curves); the hint and the Info card then show the Total length (the sum of the selected shapes). If some line ends are apart (within 2 mm), double orange circles with the gap length stay on every such place while the chain is selected (no need to bring the pointer near; Close gaps in the left menu joins them). The Info card also shows the total for shapes picked by box selection or Shift+click. "Unroll" in the Selection group of the left menu adds a horizontal straight line, as long as the whole selected line (curves and arcs included), 10 mm to the right of the selection. The original stays, and one Undo removes the new line. Use it to see the length of a curved line as a straight strip. Stitching holes on the selected line are copied onto the new line in the same order (position along the line and angle to the line); only stitch paths made entirely of selected shapes are copied, and the original holes stay.

pages.title: Trim and mirror copy
pages.body:
Trim removes the clicked span of a shape between its intersections (and endpoints), including overhanging ends. Shift+click keeps the clicked span instead. Shapes with stitching prompt before removing holes and seam settings on connected paths. Undo restores everything together.
Mirror copies the selection across an axis: select shapes, then click an axis line or two points. Holes are copied too (you can also select only holes: their mirrored copies are made with the same tool, round or diamond, on invisible helper lines); by default their slant is mirrored (reverse). Set 'Slant of mirrored holes' in Drawing options to 'Same direction' to keep the slant. Positions coincide either way. Flip horizontally/vertically follows the same setting.

pages.title: Output and printing
pages.body:
The Output card exports SVG (mm units, one group per layer, for laser software and Inkscape) and DXF R12 (Y flipped up, holes on the Stitch_Holes layer). Dots can be written as DXF POINTs. When exporting SVG, PDF or DXF, the Output card option "Merge overlapping lines on export (for laser)" (on by default) writes overlapping lines (edges shared by neighboring cells, doubled lines, the same curve with slightly shifted vertices, the same arc) only once, so the laser does not travel the same place again and again (the drawing data is not changed; for overlaps of different colors the colored line is kept; lines with a stitch-hole route and painted shapes are written as they are; the notice after exporting shows the removed length).
Choose the paper (A4/A3, portrait/landscape) and press Print. Patterns larger than the page are split with a 10 mm overlap, cross marks and page numbers. In the print dialog always choose “Actual size / 100%”.
With “Print stitching holes as dots” on, print and PDF replace each diamond hole (punched holes and diamond-shaped lines in the drawing) with a filled dot at its center; set the size with “Dot diameter”. The screen and the saved data do not change.
Calibration: place the L-shaped 100 mm scale, print it, measure X and Y on paper, enter and save. Later prints, SVG and DXF are corrected per axis. Print the scale again to confirm 100 mm.

When shapes are selected, print and export (SVG, PDF, DXF, PNG) output only the selected shapes and their stitching holes (nothing selected = the whole drawing); the notice after output says which. The tool test strip and the calibration scale always print.
Exports (SVG, PDF, DXF, PNG) open a save window where you choose the folder and name when "Choose where to save on export" is on (default on; it remembers the last place). When off, or in browsers without support (Safari, Firefox), files go to the Downloads folder. The N’s CAD format "Save" still asks for the location only the first time.

pages.title: Thickness, folds, box stitch, patchwork
pages.body:
Parts: select shapes and press Make part from selection. A part has a thickness and a stack order, editable in the Info card.
Fold lines: click two points. Angle, inner side and the neutral factor K are in the Design card. Select a fold and press Add fold allowance to create a copy extended by dL = theta x (r + K x t).
Stack correction: the part with the highest order is the outer one; its closed shapes are offset outward by the sum of inner thicknesses (folded: theta x sum t, box: sum t).
Box stitch: start it from "Box stitch" in the right-click menu (or the K key), then click stitch line A (holes through the face) then B (holes through the edge). Hole counts are matched per span (corners, curve joints) and a warning appears when the pitch differs beyond tolerance. Paired holes are connected by thin lines. Which holes stay: if neither line has stitching holes, holes are placed on both by pitch. If only one has them, they are kept and the same number is placed on the other in proportion to length (the order of clicks does not matter; if the facing lines were drawn in opposite directions, the ends that are closer are matched, and with the same number of corners the spans are matched corner by corner). If both have holes, both are redone. After the first click the hint says, for example, that the n holes of A will be copied. Make stitch line A offsets a selected edge inward by half of B's thickness.
Patchwork: seams (pairs of neighboring edges) are created automatically by "Make grid" (clicking inside an outline does the same) (there is no manual tool for pairing edges). Optimize equalizes hole counts on shared edges, keeps a gap at junctions and keeps pitches within tolerance. Suggest sizes lists three near-square cut sizes in pitch multiples; Make grid: select the outline you want a grid in (connected closed lines, dashed lines are fine) and press it (or, for an outline of solid lines, just click inside it) to fill that outline with diamonds (two slanted directions), with seams and stitch holes. The diamond width is the outline width divided by Columns (the number of whole diamonds in the middle row). The height is the outline height divided by Rows when the angle field is empty (the slant angle then follows from columns and rows); enter a number (20-80 degrees) in the angle field to fine-tune the angle (45 gives square diamonds; the height is width x tan and rows become approximate). Columns and rows may be decimals (e.g. 3.2). When stitch holes are made, the diamond side is adjusted slightly to the hole spacing so that the holes sit exactly one base pitch apart, at the same positions on both facing stitch lines (among a few sizes, the one with the fewest pieces too thin for a stitch line is chosen; the hint says so). At 45 degrees four facing holes form a square whose side is the pitch, so the cross stitch is square (away from 45 degrees it is slightly offset). The diamonds are laid out symmetrically about the centre of the outline and cut to its shape (the hint shows the diamond size and angle). Holes sit half a pitch (the stitch-line distance) inside each boundary, paired across the boundary. While the patchwork window is open the right column is folded away and the drawing area gets wider (closing the window or choosing another tool brings it back; to use a card of the right column, open it as a window from the right-click menu, e.g. Move...). Seam holes are always round; only the rim holes are diamond (they follow the rim hole type setting). The yellow dotted stitch lines and rim line are invisible helper lines that only carry the holes: they are not drawn or exported, and the holes stay. After making a grid, changing a number (columns, rows, angle, base pitch, stitch line, rim ...) rebuilds it on the spot inside the same outline (still one undo step; no rebuild after another operation). When the grid has painted areas, the paint follows its place: the point inside each old piece is looked up again in the new pieces and the same color/texture is painted there (if the size or number of diamonds changes, the color layout becomes an approximation by place; paint whose place is gone is removed and the count is shown at the bottom). Pressing "Make grid" again with the grid (or its outline) selected, or clicking a diamond, rebuilds it with the current numbers instead of stacking a second grid. To decide the size without stitch (diamond) holes, turn off "Also add seams and stitch holes (diamond holes)" just below the target width/height fields and press "Make grid" (the diamond size is exactly your target; turn it on and rebuild afterwards to add the holes). The selection right after making it includes the stitch and rim lines (invisible helper lines), so Delete removes the holes and seams too. "Optimize" does not change the seam hole type (round). Pressing Optimize re-adjusts the spacing within tolerance (double-click a line to select the connected lines). Diamonds are cut to the outline, so rounded outlines work too. A grid is only ever made inside the outline you select; with no outline selected, nothing is made. If line ends of the outline are apart so that it is not closed, no grid is made: orange circles with the gap length mark the places and you are told to fix the outline with Close gaps in the left menu (then press again). Gaps can be too small to see, so pressing the button moves and zooms the view to a gap, and pressing it again goes to the next one; even if you cannot find them, Close gaps fixes all gaps of the outline at once. "Check rim holes" checks whether the rim holes overlap a patch boundary (a visible solid line) and selects those that do (the result is also shown right after making a grid). When you change columns, rows or angle, a preview (light-blue dashed outline) and the diamond width x height and piece count appear in the hint before anything is changed. Press Enter, or stop typing for about 1 second, to confirm (when no grid exists yet and you have only selected an outline, press Enter or "Make grid"). Esc cancels the preview, and "Rebuilding the grid..." is shown while it works. When you click inside an outline that is not closed (line ends apart by up to 2 mm), or select it and press "Make grid", orange circles mark the gaps; press "Close and make" at the bottom of the screen to close the gaps and then make the grid (2 undo steps: grid, then gaps).
Click inside an outline, pattern position, texture, seam holes, rim: while the patchwork window is open (press "Click inside an outline to make a grid", or choose Patchwork in the right-click menu), click inside an outline closed by solid lines (connected lines, a closed polyline or a circle) and it is filled with the same Columns x Rows x angle diamonds as "Make grid" (no need to select the outline first). Dashed shapes are not used as boundaries. Tiny scraps (under 5% of a diamond) are skipped. To slide the whole grid up, down, left or right and balance how it looks, type a number in "Pattern position: left-right / up-down (mm)" (+ = right / down) or press the ← → ↑ ↓ buttons (each press moves by "Amount per button press", 0.5 mm at first). The grid stays cut at the outline of the shape, and it is rebuilt on the spot (still one undo step). "Reset pattern position to 0" brings back the symmetric layout. Moving a made grid with the keyboard arrows would push it past the outline, so adjust the position here instead. Choose "Pattern texture A / B" to tile a leather photo on each of the two colors (changing it later regenerates the pieces). If "Also add seams and stitch holes" is checked (default), for cross-stitching each piece gets a stitch line (an invisible helper line) shrunk inward from its edge by half the base pitch, and the stitch holes go on it. Holes are never placed on the boundary; holes facing each other across the boundary are paired (neighboring stitch lines are registered as seams, and the pitch is matched with the same calculation as Optimize). If "No diamond holes within 2.5 mm of an edge" is checked (default), rim diamond holes are not made closer than 2.5 mm to the edge (uncheck it to allow). Outer-edge holes: while "Also punch stitch holes around the outer edge" is checked (default; "Also add seams and stitch holes" must be checked too), a line (an invisible helper line) is made by moving the outline inward by "Outer stitch line: distance from the edge" (2.5 mm at first), and holes of the "Rim hole type" (diamond at first) are punched on it. The corners of that line are rounded by "Corner rounding radius" (8 mm at first; 0 = no rounding), and the hole spacing is "Outer diamond hole spacing" (4 mm at first; adjusted slightly so it closes evenly). Holes that already sit at the ends of the seams on that line are kept, and the gaps between them are filled evenly. Outer holes are nudged aside or left out so they never touch solid lines (the outline, the pieces’ lines, circles). If the corner radius is too large for the shape it is made smaller until it fits. A distance so small that holes would touch the edge line, or under 2.5 mm while "No diamond holes within 2.5 mm of an edge" is checked, makes nothing.

pages.title: File formats (import and export)
pages.body:
Open or drag-and-drop: .json (this CAD's document), .svg (path, line, rect, circle, ellipse, polyline, polygon, text, transforms, mm/cm/in/px units), .dxf (LINE, CIRCLE, ARC, LWPOLYLINE/POLYLINE with bulge, SPLINE, TEXT/MTEXT, INSERT blocks, $INSUNITS). Imported shapes are added to the current drawing; broken elements are dropped and counted. SVG <g id> becomes a layer.
Export: SVG (mm, per-layer groups, optional fill), DXF R12, PDF (A4/A3, tiling, calibration, ASCII text only), PNG (dpi, optional transparency, up to 50 M pixels), JSON.
"Save selected shapes as" in the Save menu writes only the selected shapes (with their stitching holes, paths, parts and fills) to a new file with a name you choose. The current drawing and its Ctrl+S target stay as they are.

pages.title: Leathercraft CAD and Beam Studio
pages.body:
Target “Leathercraft CAD” writes DXF with layers LineType_01 (pattern), LineType_02 (hardware), LineType_03 (guide), holes on Stitch_Holes, origin at the lower-left corner. Opening a Leathercraft CAD DXF maps LineType_NN back to layers, restores Stitch_Holes circles/diamonds as stitching holes and recovers arcs from polyline approximations (toggle in the Output card).
Target “Beam Studio” fixes SVG colors: cut lines black (closed shapes offset outward by half the kerf), stitch holes and hardware holes red circles; guides and hardware outlines omitted (add engraving in Beam Studio). In Beam Studio assign black = cut, red = holes, blue = engrave. PNG gives the same drawing in black and white for engraving.

pages.title: 3D folding and three views
pages.body:
Toggle with the 3D button. Closed shapes of parts become panels with thickness, split by fold lines, and rotate by the fold angle as the slider goes from 0% (open) to 100% (closed). Play loops the motion. The fold direction follows the fold line's inner-side setting (grain faces meet). Parts with a higher stack order sit on top of the lower ones.
Left drag rotates, right drag (or Shift) pans, wheel zooms. Quad view shows front, top and right orthographic views plus the free view.
Panels overlapping when closed are drawn red and counted (neighbors joined by a fold are excluded). Views SVG exports third-angle front/top/right views in mm; Print views prints them. Without WebGL a simple painter renderer is used.

pages.title: From three views to a solid (front / top / right)
pages.body:
Draw the front, top and right views, then check the result as a solid. Follow the steps in order.
[Setup] Tick “3 views (front / top / right)” at the top. Three boxes appear: the front view at the lower left, the top view right above it, and the right view to its right.
[Choosing the boxes yourself] Draw a straight rectangle, select it and press “Use selected rectangle as box”. A rectangle in the front area becomes the front box (depth from the “Depth” field); one in the top area sets the width and depth; one in the right area sets the height and depth. The other boxes are made from it, and the choice is saved with the file. “Reset boxes” returns to the standard size.
[Step 1 Draw the front] Draw the front shape inside the Front view box (a closed shape such as a rectangle, circle or polyline). Dotted lines run from its corners and ends: vertical ones into the top box and horizontal ones into the right box. They mark where the other views line up with the front view.
[Step 2 Make the top and right outlines] Type the depth (front to back, in mm) into “Depth” and press “Make top & right views”. From the box enclosing everything in the front view and that depth, the outlines (rectangles) of the top and right views are drawn. Nothing is made if the same rectangles already exist. Undo removes them.
[Step 3 Add the details] Draw the details inside the top and right boxes, following the dotted lines. Clicking near a dotted line pulls the point exactly onto it, sideways or up-and-down (this works even when Snap is off). In the top and right boxes the depth in mm is shown next to the cursor. The depth you draw in the top view travels along the 45° line at the upper right into the right view (the bottom edge of the top box and the left edge of the right box are the near side).
[Solid at the upper right] Once the front view has a closed shape, a small solid is always shown in the empty upper-right area (where the 45° line is) and changes as you draw. Drag inside it to turn it.
[Step 4 Check it as a solid] Press 3D at the top and a solid built from your three views appears. Left-drag rotates, right-drag (or Shift+drag) pans, the wheel zooms. In the “3D (folding)” card on the right, choose Quad view to see it next to the front, top and right views. “Views SVG” and “Print views” use the same solid.
[How it works] The height of the front shape is cut into thin slices; each slice is trimmed by the top shape and the right shape, then they are stacked. If the top or right box has no closed shape, a rectangle is assumed.
[Keep in mind] The boxes are only guides, not shapes (they are not saved or exported). They grow automatically to fit what you draw. The near-side lines (bottom edge of the top box, left edge of the right box) stay put unless the front view grows far upward or to the right. Small hollows, holes and multiple parts cannot be turned into a solid yet. This feature is still being built.

pages.title: Three views (4 panes): separate sheets
pages.body:
Draw the front, top and right views on separate sheets (tabs) and see all of them at once in four panes. There are no boxes or 45° line; the sheets are linked only by dotted lines.
[Turning it on] Tick “3 views (4 panes)” at the top. The current drawing becomes the Front sheet, and Top and Right sheets (tabs) are created for you. The screen splits into four panes: top view at the upper left, front view at the lower left, right view at the lower right, and the solid at the upper right.
[Drawing] Click the pane you want to draw in; that sheet becomes the active one (its border turns gold and the tab switches). Then draw as usual. Each pane can be zoomed and panned on its own.
[Sheet directions] The Top sheet has a horizontal “near side line”; above it is further back (the distance from the line is the depth). The Right sheet has a vertical near side line; to its right is further back. The Front sheet is a normal drawing.
[Dotted lines] Lines coming from the other sheets: the x of front corners appear as vertical lines on the Top sheet, front heights as horizontal lines on the Right sheet, Top-sheet depths as vertical lines on the Right sheet, and Right-sheet depths as horizontal lines on the Top sheet. Clicking near a dotted line pulls the point onto it. Light-blue lines on the other sheets follow your cursor.
[Solid] The upper-right pane always shows the solid built from the three sheets and changes as you draw. Drag inside it to turn it. The 3D button, Views SVG and Print views use the same solid.
[Saving] Saving from any of the sheet tabs puts all three sheets into one file. Loading it brings the three tabs back.
[Keep in mind] “3 views (4 panes)” and “3 views (front / top / right)” (the box method) cannot be on at the same time. Turning 4 panes off keeps the sheets (tabs). Switching from 4 panes to the box method moves the shapes on the top and right sheets into the top and right boxes of the front sheet; turning 4 panes back on returns them to the sheets. Small hollows, holes and multiple parts cannot be turned into a solid yet.

pages.title: Hardware library and binder mechanisms
pages.body:
Choose a category and an item in the Hardware card, adjust the size parameters (typical values; verify the ones marked) and the angle, press Place and click on the drawing. The outline symbol goes to the Hardware layer; mounting holes (rivets, snap posts, screws) go to the Hardware layer. Placed hardware also appears in 3D as a box or cylinder on its panel, follows folding and is included in collision checks.
For binder mechanisms pick a standard (Micro5, Mini6, A6, Bible, A5, A5 Slim, A4, Franklin...) and a ring diameter. Hole pitches, first-to-last span and refill sizes come from N's factory's standards table (data/binder/*.json); plate and rivet sizes are estimates you can overwrite. Plan/side/front drawings are generated from the JSON. The required spine width = ring diameter + plate thickness + 2 × leather thickness + 2 mm play.
Spine simulation: choose the spine shape (square = two 90° folds with the bend radius you enter; round = a half circle around the rings, bend radius = half the inner width automatically, supporter curved inside the cover), then in the binder section, enter ring ID, wire, plate thickness, cover leather, supporter thickness, clearance and bend radius; the closed section (ring OD + clearance = inner width, 90° fold allowances both ends) gives the spine width with a section drawing. Enter a spine you measured by wrapping real leather to derive the clearance, then reuse it for other sizes. "Apply to recipe spine" feeds the notebook recipe.
With "Edit sizes" you can enter the base plate, rings (inner/outer/wire/embed per size) and mounting holes yourself; they are saved in this browser and applied at once to drawings, 3D and the spine simulation. "Save as a new product" adds a named maker variant of the same standard. To put them in the public data, export the three CSV files and send them.
"Draw the cover pattern from this result" in the spine simulation uses the computed spine width plus the top/bottom and fore-edge margins to draw, in a new tab, the cover outline (a part with the leather thickness), two fold lines and the binder centered on the spine (add pockets yourself).

pages.title: Part library, tabs and reuse
pages.body:
Part library: built-in parts (card pocket, pen holder, ring base, D-ring tab) and your own parts can be placed with adjustable variables (W, H...). Select shapes, name them and press Register to store them with holes, paths and part info (localStorage). Export/Import moves the library between PCs as .nscad-lib.json.
Tabs: open several drawings and switch with tabs (undo, selection and view per tab). Copy or move the selection to another tab.
Clipboard: Ctrl/⌘+C copies the selection as text; Ctrl/⌘+V pastes in another tab, window or PC. IDs are reassigned and missing layers are created. Scale lets you resize while pasting. Sources are kept in the document's provenance.

pages.title: Ask AI
pages.body:
Send a question or request from the AI card; Claude replies with text and proposed actions. Nothing changes until you press Apply (undo available). “Attach the current drawing” sends a summary (mm, hole counts, thickness, selected ids; no images).
Enter the server URL and passphrase in AI settings (the server is the Cloudflare Worker in worker/; the API key stays on the server). The card shows an estimate before sending, the real token usage and cost after, and the monthly total.
Preset buttons: review the pattern, stitching margin, card-case draft, how-to. The last 20 exchanges are kept on this PC.

pages.title: Auto design from a recipe
pages.body:
Fill the Recipe card (product, cards or refill and ring size, thickness, stitch style, pitch, paper) and press Generate. A new tab gets the full pattern (cut lines, stitch lines with holes, folds, labels, part thickness) and is checked immediately.
Rules: card 85.60×53.98×0.76 mm; pocket = card + 3 mm play, width + cards×0.76. Edge stitch: stitch line 3 mm from the edge, no allowance; turned: 6 mm allowance. Notebook: height = refill + 10, spine = ring + plate + 2×leather + 2, width = 2×(refill width + 3) + spine + fold allowance.
Check lists unconnected lines, parts outside the paper, seam hole mismatches, collisions when closed and zero-length lines; selecting one jumps to it. Thread estimate (length×4+100 mm) is in the stitching card. Products without rules can be drafted by the AI and checked the same way. The final decision is always yours.

pages.title: Underlay images and tracing
pages.body:
Import a scanned pattern or sketch (PNG/JPEG) from the Underlay card or drop it on the canvas. It sits on the guide layer and is stored in this PC's IndexedDB (the document keeps only an id).
Scale: use the scan dpi, or click two points on the image and enter their real distance. Opacity and angle are adjustable; locking makes it unselectable.
Manual tracing: draw lines, pen paths or polylines over it (no snapping to the image).
Auto trace: set threshold (empty = auto), simplify tolerance and minimum area, press Preview, check the red contours and Apply to add them to the pattern layer.

pages.title: Drafts from photos, sketches and 3D
pages.body:
From a photo or sketch: import it as an underlay, tick “Attach the underlay photo” in the AI card, enter the reference width and press the photo preset. The AI proposes parts and shapes (setRecipe / addShapes); after Apply you can run the recipe pipeline and the check. Estimated sizes are marked as estimates. Photos are not stored on the server.
From 3D: panels made with fold lines can be flattened with “Unfold to a new tab” in the 3D card; edges not on a fold get the given allowance (arbitrary stacked solids are out of scope).

pages.title: Color simulation
pages.body:
In the “Fill colors (leather, thread, hardware)” card choose a leather color per part (16 swatches or #RRGGBB) and a thread color per stitched path (92 Vinymo MBT colors, searchable by number and Japanese name, pin favorites). In 2D closed part shapes are tinted and holes take the thread color; 3D uses the part color on panels.
Color sets can be saved by name in the document and switched. “Colored SVG” exports fills and thread colors; “3D as PNG” saves the current 3D view. Leather texture: in the Fill colors card’s "Leather texture", search a leather by name (e.g. ALASKA pink), select a part’s shape and press "Apply texture to selected parts"; a seamless leather photo (280 Kawamura leathers) is tiled over it. "Texture tile size (mm)": leave it blank to use each photo’s own real size (recorded per leather; 30 mm when unknown), or enter a number to tile every texture at that size (saved per document). MARGOT FOG was rebuilt from the supplier’s original photos as one large sheet (about 330 mm) of randomly rotated, edge-blended pieces, so the same pattern does not repeat in a regular grid. Apply "None" to return to the flat color. A closed shape outside any part gets the texture itself (a shape’s own texture wins over its part’s). "Colored SVG" embeds the photos; 3D shows the photo too (the top and bottom of each panel, and the faces of a solid built from the three views; panel edges and non-WebGL browsers use the average color). In the 4-pane three-view mode the other sheets are textured as well, and outlines made by "Make top and right views" inherit the front shape’s texture. The small solid in the corner uses the average color.
Erasing metal colors: click "Clear metal color" without selecting anything to enter erase mode. Click a line shown in a metal color to clear that line’s group (the loop or the hardware group), or click a painted area to remove its metal fill (leather fills stay). Esc to finish.
The line color "white" shows white on the dark screen. SVG exports the colors you set as they are (lasers change the process by color); tick "Black and white (SVG)" in the Output card only when you want monochrome. In PDF, PNG and printing (paper), white lines are drawn black. Stitch diamonds with no color are red in SVG, so they differ from the black cut lines.
To remove the painting in a selection, select shapes (a box selection or Select all also works) and choose "Remove all painting in the selection" from the right-click menu, or press the button of the same name in the Paint colors card. The painted areas (leather, texture, metal, transparent) of the selected shapes and the leather color, texture and metal color set on them are removed together (painting on shapes you did not select stays; Undo is one step). To clear the whole drawing, use "Clear all painted areas".

pages.title: Keyboard shortcuts
pages.body:
All the keyboard shortcuts on one page.
Ctrl/⌘+Z undo / Ctrl+Y, ⌘⇧Z redo / Delete, Backspace delete / Ctrl/⌘+D duplicate / Ctrl/⌘+S save / Ctrl/⌘+O open / Ctrl/⌘+C copy / Ctrl/⌘+X cut / Ctrl/⌘+V paste (work with shapes selected even when a button has focus; inside text fields they act on text) / Ctrl/⌘+A select all / Esc cancel and return to the Select tool (the pen steps back one node at a time, then Select) / Enter finish polyline or pen / Space+drag pan / Shift constrain / Alt(⌥)+click single hole / F1 shortcuts / ? help.
Mouse: wheel zoom, middle button pan, double-click finishes the pen or adds a node. Trackpad: pinch zoom, two fingers pan.
Browser keys such as F5, Ctrl+R (reload), Ctrl+W, F12 and Ctrl+F keep working as usual.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.body:
Common problems and fixes.
Nothing works from file://: make sure all files sit next to index.html; otherwise serve over http (e.g. py -m http.server).
Prints are not actual size: set the print dialog to Actual size / 100%, print the calibration scale, measure X and Y and save the correction.
Safari does not save: allow downloads when asked, then try again.
3D is black: WebGL is disabled; the simple renderer takes over.
AI unavailable: set the server URL and passphrase; deploy the Worker as in worker/README.md.
Cannot place holes: text, dimensions, folds and underlays cannot carry holes; closed shapes must really close.

pages.title: Video tutorials (Show me)
pages.body:
Press “Show me” in Help and the app performs the steps on screen (fake cursor, highlighted buttons, captions). Change the speed, pause, or switch to “Do it myself” to get only prompts. Scripts live in tutorials/*.json; four are included: drawing, stitching, pen, output.
MP4 files are produced by the Playwright recording script (C:\dev\leather-cad-tools\record_tutorials.mjs) and embedded in the manual when present in docs/videos/.

pages.title: Voice control
pages.body:
Hold the microphone button and speak to switch tools or edit. Typing the same words in the box below does the same.
Tools: line, circle, arc, bezier/curve, pen, polyline, text, dimension, fillet, chamfer, offset, trim, mirror, fold, koma, seam, stitch/holes
With numbers: "line 100 mm angle 30", "circle radius 15", "offset 3 inside/outside", "chamfer 5", "stitch 4 mm variable", "zoom 200", "grid 2 mm"
Editing: undo, redo, delete, copy, flip horizontal/vertical, select all, save, SVG/DXF/PDF, print
View: 3D, 2D, help, zoom in, zoom out, fit
When unsure, 2–3 candidates appear; tap one. Delete, save and print ask first: say "yes" to run or "no" to cancel.
Sentences outside the grammar ("check the allowance of this card case") go straight to the AI card.
Settings: hold vs tap mode, read-back on/off (off by default), mic level meter (warns on prolonged silence). Speech is processed by the browser's recognition (Chrome/Edge/Safari use cloud recognition). Browsers without it can use the text box only.

pages.title: My designs (importing Leathercraft CAD)
pages.body:
Open a .lcc file (Leathercraft CAD save) and it becomes an N's CAD drawing with lines, arcs, Béziers, text, dimensions and stitch holes. Holes are re-attached to the nearest line and the tools (diamond/round, pitch, hole size) are recreated.
The library card's "My designs" lists past designs converted by tools/import_lcc.js (filter with the search box). "Open in new tab" loads the whole drawing; "Place into this drawing" pastes it at the center (scaled by the paste scale). The list is available only over http.
The tendencies of past designs (pitch, hole size, common corner radii, text size) are summarized in data/style.json and used as the recipe's default pitch and as context for the AI panel. A summary appears under the list.
Unreadable elements (broken files, elliptical arcs) are counted; broken files are listed in designs/_failed.json.

pages.title: Stitching: closed seams and reverse direction
pages.body:
Circles and closed polylines do not duplicate the first and last hole. The seam has an arc-length position of 0 mm in either direction. The bisector corner option also applies at the seam, with the tool slant added to its angle.
Alt/Option-click places one hole. Switching direction and adding holes does not duplicate the seam hole.

pages.title: Node editing and numeric drawing
pages.body: Click the selected pen path to insert a node. Removing an inserted node without editing it restores the original curve. Drag nodes or handles; hold Alt (Option) to edit one handle independently. For lines, circles and arcs, click a starting point and complete the geometry in the bottom input. Use x,y for absolute coordinates, @dx,dy for relative coordinates and 50<30 for length and angle. Enter a radius for circles, or radius, start angle and end angle for arcs. F1 opens shortcuts; ? opens help.

pages.title: How we handle personal information and analytics
pages.body:
■ Drawing contents: Nothing about your drawing (shapes, text, dimensions, file names) is sent to the operator (N's factory) automatically. Saved drawings, phrases and edited hardware sizes stay in your browser only. The operator sees a drawing only when you hand over a "Bug log" file yourself (see below).
■ Registration: Printing, saving files and exporting require registration. When you register, your email address, nickname (optional) and consent are sent to the operator's Google spreadsheet, and a confirmation email is returned. After that, each time you use a function, the date and time, the function name (a short code) and the build number are recorded against your email address. The purpose is to confirm your registration and to see how often each function is used. Only the operator sees this, and it is not shared with third parties except where required by law. To delete your registration, email the operator. Your browser on this device keeps your registration status and any usage records not yet sent.
■ Analytics (public version only): Google Analytics counts page views and how often each function is used (buttons, tools, menu items and cards opened). Only the name of the function (a short code) and the count are sent; shapes, text, dimensions, file names and numbers you type are never sent. The operator's own device is not counted. Google may use cookies or similar to tell visits from the same device apart. When opened locally via file://, analytics are not sent.
■ Feedback: Only when you press "Feedback" and send, what you wrote (type, message, contact), the build number and screen information (shown before sending, and you can turn it off) go to the operator. Your drawing contents are not sent.
■ Bug log: To investigate a problem, the "Bug log" button in the header saves a file on your computer containing your drawing itself, your last 300 operations (click positions, the shapes hit, keys pressed), your browser type, screen size and the build number. It is only saved; nothing is sent automatically. Whether to hand it to the operator is up to you. A file you hand over is used only to investigate the problem and is not shared with third parties. Text typed into input fields is not recorded, but text, dimensions and file names inside the drawing are included. If there is something you do not want others to see, check before handing it over.
■ Voice input: When you use it, your voice may be sent to your browser's speech recognition (in Chrome, Edge and similar, the browser vendor's servers). It does not reach the operator.
■ AI consult: Available only when you enter a server URL and passphrase in the AI card. What is sent: the last 20 messages of the conversation; the drawing information (shapes, layer names, part names, etc.) when "Attach the current drawing" is checked (it is on by default); and a shrunk underlay photo when "Attach the underlay photo" is checked. These go through that server to an AI (Anthropic's Claude). If you enter nothing, nothing is sent.
